name: xblocks
title: Plot Contiguous Blocks along x Axis

origin.description: Shade contiguous blocks along the time index of a zoo series.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A zoo series. The blocks are placed at index(x).

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Defaults to x. A non-function is replaced by coredata(y) before the default method. A function is applied to the index, not to the data.
Passed to xblocks.default: col, border, ybottom, ytop, height, and last.step.

origin.details: Numeric core data is coverage: a missing value is a gap and a finite value is a block. A logical FALSE becomes a missing color after rle, so that run is still a rectangle but it is not filled. The last block extends by median(diff(tail(index))).
origin.value: NULL, invisibly. The rectangles are drawn with rect. The check records their coordinates.
origin.example:
flow <- zoo(c(1, NA, 3, 3, NA, 8), 1:6)
xblocks(flow, col = "darkgray", ybottom = 0, height = 2)

translation.description: Shade contiguous blocks along the index of a Zoo series.
translation.usage: xblocks(x, y=None, col=None, border=None, ybottom=None, ytop=None, height=None, last_step=None, ylog=False, draw=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Zoo series. The blocks are placed at its index.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Defaults to x. A callable is applied to the index. Anything else is the core data.

arguments.name: col, border, ybottom, ytop, height, last_step
arguments.text: Same block rules as xblocks_default. ylog is par("ylog") and is false unless set.

arguments.name: draw
arguments.text: True draws the rectangles with Matplotlib. False returns the coordinates and is the timed call.

translation.details: The zoo method only chooses the index and the y values. The rectangle arithmetic is xblocks_default. The comparison is that geometry. The SVG draws the coverage blocks and the series on top of them.
translation.value: A dict with left, right, bottom, top, col, and border. With draw=True it also holds the Matplotlib axes.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.plot import xblocks
flow = Zoo(np.array([1, np.nan, 3, 3, np.nan, 8], dtype=float), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
xblocks(flow, col="darkgray", ybottom=0, ytop=10, draw=True)
